featured_reviews.name: 光頭小伍
featured_reviews.review_text:
走進孟買的心臟，你會來到一個讓世界又震撼又敬佩的地方——Dharavi。這裡面積僅約1.75平方公里，卻容納了數十萬人口，是亞洲最密集的社區之一。但如果你只用「貧民窟」來定義它，那就太小看這裡了。

在狹窄巷弄之間，藏著驚人的經濟能量。回收、皮革、紡織、陶器，一間間小工坊日夜運轉，創造出數億美元的產值，產品甚至銷往世界各地。這裡沒有華麗辦公室，卻有最真實的創業精神；沒有資源優勢，卻用雙手打造無限可能。

來自印度各地的人們在此落腳，不同語言、宗教與文化交織，形成獨特的生命力。儘管面對擁擠與衛生挑戰，他們依然努力生活、努力工作，用韌性撐起整個城市的運轉。

達拉維不是悲情的象徵，而是一面鏡子，讓人看見人在困境中依然可以發光。走一趟，你會重新理解什麼叫做努力，什麼叫做希望。
featured_reviews.review_translated_text:
Step into the heart of Mumbai, and you'll find a place that both shocks and inspires awe—Dharavi. Spanning only about 1.75 square kilometers, it houses hundreds of thousands of people, making it one of the most densely populated communities in Asia. But to define it merely as a "slum" would be a gross underestimation.

Hidden within its narrow alleyways is an astonishing economic energy. Recycling, leather, textiles, pottery—small workshops operate day and night, generating hundreds of millions of dollars in revenue, with products sold worldwide. Here, there are no glamorous offices, but the most genuine entrepreneurial spirit; no resource advantages, but limitless possibilities created with their own hands.

People from all over India have settled here, their diverse languages, religions, and cultures intertwining to create a unique vitality. Despite facing overcrowding and sanitation challenges, they persevere, working hard and resiliently keeping the city running.

Dharavi is not a symbol of tragedy, but a mirror reflecting the light that shines even in adversity. A visit will give you a new understanding of the meaning of hard work and hope.

featured_reviews.name: Brett Hansen
featured_reviews.review_text:
We joined the ethical walking tour of Dharavi slums with Reality Tours & Travel and it was one of the most eye opening and meaningful experiences of our time in Mumbai, India.

Our guide Diksha was excellent. She is a young Gen Z woman who is incredibly wise, well informed and very articulate. She explained the social, economic and cultural realities of Dharavi with clarity and compassion, and was always happy to answer questions along the way.

What I appreciated most about this tour is that it focuses primarily on the businesses and industries operating within Dharavi rather than treating it like a spectacle. We saw small scale recycling operations, leather workshops, pottery areas and many other hardworking micro industries. It was fascinating to learn how much manufacturing and production takes place here. At times we also walked through incredibly narrow pathways between homes, sometimes only about a metre wide, which gave a sense of just how densely populated the area is.

Dharavi has an estimated population of between 700,000 and 1 million people living in only about 2.1 square kilometres, so the energy and activity is intense. People work extremely hard. Many workers come from other regions of India, sending money home to their families and only seeing them once or twice a year. Some sleep at their workplaces and work 12 to 15 hour days. It is a tough life and seeing this reality firsthand is humbling.

One of the most confronting things we learned is that materials produced in Dharavi are sometimes used by high end international brands. However, the origin is often labelled simply as “Made in India” rather than Dharavi because of the stigma attached to the area. That was heartbreaking to hear given the skill and effort of the people working there.

Photography and video are not allowed on the tour, which is completely fair and respectful. It keeps the focus on learning rather than treating people’s lives as a spectacle.

Another reason to support this tour is that 80 percent of the profits go back into local education programs run by the organisation. While schooling in India is compulsory, class sizes can be around one teacher to 50 students. Reality Tours supports supplementary learning including English and IT classes, along with scholarships for local students.

The tour was scheduled for about 90 minutes but ended up running for closer to two hours and fifteen minutes, so we were definitely tired by the end, but it was absolutely worth it.

If you want to better understand a part of Mumbai that many visitors never see, this slum tour is thoughtful, respectful and genuinely educational. It reminds you that there are whole worlds of experience beyond our own daily lives, and that they are worth learning about with empathy and respect.

name: Mumbai Tours by Sukanya
description: Private Tour Guide for Mumbai Sukanya, is licensed with seven years' experience, is ready to show you the city like never before. Her deep knowledge of Mumbai's history and culture, combined with her fun facts and stories, will make your sightseeing adventure unforgettable. As a visiting faculty teaching travel and tourism, Sukanya is eager to share her passion for Mumbai with you. Book a private tour and embrace the true spirit of Mumbai.

featured_reviews.name: Plamen Chavdarov
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had the pleasure of spending six wonderful hours exploring Mumbai with my guide, Sukanya, and I could not have asked for a better experience. From the moment she picked me up at my hotel, she made me feel welcomed, comfortable, and excited to discover her city. Sukanya has an exceptional ability to combine deep knowledge with engaging storytelling — she shared fascinating historical and cultural insights without ever making the tour feel overwhelming or academic.

What truly stood out was her warmth, enthusiasm, and genuine love for Mumbai. She brought the city to life in a way that was both informative and highly entertaining, adapting the pace and content perfectly to my interests. Every stop felt meaningful, and her explanations added depth to places I might otherwise have simply passed by.

Sukanya is professional, personable, and incredibly knowledgeable, yet never boring — a rare and wonderful combination. I highly recommend her to anyone wanting to experience Mumbai through the eyes of someone who truly understands and loves her city.

featured_reviews.name: Rebecca Lee
featured_reviews.review_text:
Sukanya was an excellent tour guide during my recent trip to Mumbai, in which we did no fewer than 5 different tours together, covering different parts of Mumbai heritage and Indian culture. She was unfailingly professional, very friendly and personable, and deeply knowledgeable about Indian history and culture. I highly recommend Sukanya for any visitors to the city who are looking for an experienced and engaging tour guide to make their trip to Mumbai unforgettable.

I loved how willing she was to adapt the tours to my personal interests to make each experience relevant and memorable for me - I have a great love of architecture, and Sukanya would often point out more architectural history and detail as we walked along for my interest. She also incorporated information spontaneously based on what we were seeing each day and the local vendors we met on our walks, which really made each tour come alive with local colour.

Together we did tours of Art Deco buildings along Marine Drive, "Mumbai at Dawn" covering the early morning markets, the Dharavi slum, a Heritage and History tour of Fort, and a street food crawl. Seeing the markets of Mumbai at dawn was such a special experience, and a real highlight of my trip. Not only did I learn so much on our tours, but we also had great fun together, and many laughs! By the end of the week, it truly felt like I was being shown around Mumbai by an old friend. Thank you so much Sukanya, and hope to see you on my next India trip.

featured_reviews.name: Peggy Seaver
featured_reviews.review_text:
My husband and I had the greatest pleasure of having Sukanya as our tour guide during a visit to Mumbai. Sukanya was the best tour guide we have ever had in our decades of travel. She is also one of the nicest people you could every hope to meet!

In addition to being lovely and intelligent, she is articulate and has an exceptional command of the English language. She is formally educated, holding a graduate degree in the social sciences and serves as a visiting professor at a local Mumbai university.

Initially, we were interested in the typical walking tour the heritage buildings, Elephanta Caves, and other standard tourist sites, which we greatly enjoyed.

After getting to know us better, she offered an early morning (5:30 a.m.) visit to the distribution centres of the daily newspapers as well as home milk delivery!  It was so amazing to see this in action.

We then visited the produce and flower distribution centres.  The produce was exceptionally fresh.  Lastly, we visited the Dhobi Ghat which is the world's largest open air laundromat.  It was an unforgettable experience.

Sukanya was very well versed in current events of Mumbai and India. She had so much information to share with us and we throughly enjoyed meeting her!

featured_reviews.name: abhimanyu singh
featured_reviews.review_text:
We had a wonderful experience touring Mumbai with Sukanya. She curated a fantastic journey through iconic landmarks like the Gateway of India, Victoria Terminus, Mani Bhavan, Dhobi Ghat, and the Prince of Wales Museum, bringing each place alive with stories and deep historical context.
Sukanya is incredibly knowledgeable, articulate, and passionate about the city. What truly stood out was how effortlessly she connected different parts of Mumbai—its history, culture, and everyday life—making the tour both insightful and engaging.
Highly recommend her to anyone looking to truly understand Mumbai beyond just sightseeing. An enriching and memorable experience!

featured_reviews.name: Bina Raval
featured_reviews.review_text: We were on a whistlestop tour of Mumbai, so glad to have Sukanya guide us around the key places to see. She was able to fit so much in and tailor the short time we had to really give us a feel of what life is like in Mumbai. Thanks for a lovely day and memorable introduction to Mumbai.

featured_reviews.name: Mark Cracknell
featured_reviews.review_text:
We had a wonderful time with Sukanya as our tour guide!

She tells the story of a historical site, market or neighbourhood in a fun and engaging way that educates you and makes the city and its history come alive.

As a Mumbaikar, she knows the city inside and out, and made our vist very enjoyable while keeping us safe and secure at all times.

featured_reviews.name: Katherine Dinsdale
featured_reviews.review_text: Our Full-Day Mumbai tour with Sukanya was indeed FULL. Our talented guide did a great job helping us navigate various ticket counters and street crossings, all the while providing good commentary on the sites, as well as many aspects of life in Mumbai. She was knowledgeable and willing to answer questions on every subject. I particularly enjoyed her passionate interpretation of all the carved Hindu deities at the temple at Elephanta Caves. My husband has hearing loss and it was a challenge to hear her, especially with a great deal of ambient noise throughout the day--we were in Mumbai, after all. Sukanya worked hard to accommodate him. We loved having lunch together at a Parsi restaurant midway through our day. Well-paced and well done. Thank you, Sukanya.

featured_reviews.name: Helen Hitchcock
featured_reviews.review_text: Sukanya took myself and my group of ladies on a Mumbai City Tour, she was wonderful and facilitated many personal requests as we had group members who were born in the city. She was kind and knowledgeable and would definitely recommend her. I already have made my next booking.

name: Be the Local Tours
description:
We have been Born & Brought-up in Aamchee ('OUR') Mumbai and hence know it like the back of our hand! So we boldly venture down its small lanes to Explore stuff that otherwise just goes UNdiscovered. You will be in for many of surprises - plenty of amazing stuff, people and variety of activities!
Being The Local’s, we can offer you a fascinating 'getaway' that gives you a ringside view of the 'Madness and Magic' of MUMBAI.
address: 5-154B, Municipal Bldg, Main Road, Dharavi, Mumbai, Maharashtra 400017

featured_reviews.name: Adrienne Ryan
featured_reviews.review_text:
A very kind and knowledgeable Adnan, our guide, took us on a tour of the ‘slum’.

As he told us, the guides themselves have to live in the slum and haw to be in education. Adnan was currently doing his Masters in computer science - so a smart young man.
He also explained to us that the term ‘slum’ does not have the same meaning in India as it would in the UK, for example. The word in India refers to the style of building.

In many ways the tour was confronting but with the careful and insightful guidance of Adnan we learned that the residents of the slum are extraordinarily proud of their homes and work.

They work hard and, as a result, the annual turnover of the 2.7 square miles area is around $750,000 - $1 billion!

We came away with a sense of understanding and knowledge that would not be possible from afar.

featured_reviews.name: Karla Kinserdal
featured_reviews.review_text: Amazing, fascinating and educational experience. I booked through my hotel (Four Seasons) and went for a 4 hour guided tour for one person. The guide Adnan was super friendly and knowledgeable. He answered all my questions and was patient and helpful the entire time. The people seem to have a strong sense of community and care for each other. They’re friendly and smiling. Highly recommend this experience.

featured_reviews.name: Debbie Harrison
featured_reviews.review_text:
This tour was beyond my highest expectations! My hotel concierge recommended doing the tour through Be The Local Tours because of the direct link to the area and it was the best choice! My guide Amaan (a resident from
this community) , provided so much great information. He was friendly, accommodating and very knowledgeable.
Happy to answer all my questions. The tour gave me an outstanding appreciation of the slum community and how it all works on a daily basis for so many millions of people. I feel more enlightened and impressed for having had the privilege to visit . Highly recommend Amaan and the Be The Local Tours team for this tour.

featured_reviews.name: L De Wit
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Truly Eye‑Opening Experience in Dharavi

Our tour through Dharavi was one of the most memorable and impactful experiences we had during our time in Mumbai. What made it truly exceptional was our guide, Razak. Having grown up in Dharavi — and still living there today — he shared the neighborhood with us with incredible authenticity, pride, and deep personal insight.

Razak’s connection to Dharavi is truly admirable. He showed us the area not as tourists passing through, but as guests in a vibrant “city within the city.” At every step, he managed the perfect balance: giving us a close look into daily life, the local industries, and the strong community spirit, without ever making us feel like we were intruding on anyone’s privacy. His respect for the people who call Dharavi home was evident in every story he told.

Walking through the narrow lanes, seeing the craftsmanship, the creativity, and the resilience of the community was an experience we will never forget. It completely changed our perspective of Dharavi and of Mumbai as a whole.

We would highly recommend this tour to anyone who wants to see more of Mumbai than the usual highlights. It was a unique and meaningful experience — thanks to Razak, who made it personal, respectful, and truly insightful.

featured_reviews.name: Siwei Cheng
featured_reviews.review_text: Great tour from Adnan who patiently took our family through an informative, eye-opening and uplifting walk in and out of various alleyways, factories, eateries within Dharavi to get a first account of the hard working community within Asia’s largest slum. Thank you Adnan, and highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: Savi G. (Savylg)
featured_reviews.review_text:
I went on a guided tour of Dharavi during my recent stay in Mumbai. Faiz, from Be the Local Tours, was my guide and he was just fabulous. As he walked with me through Dharavi, he spoke with me as if we were old friends. As he explained the inner workings of this city within a city - pointing out the different districts and businesses found within this 2x2 square kilometer area - I was just mesmerized. What an amazing place - I am so honoured to have had an opportunity to visit and learn about life in Dharavi.

A labyrinth of narrow lanes and crowded spaces and a symphony of colors, sounds, and smells. I couldn't help but be captivated by the resourcefulness and creativity of that little community. Every corner of Dharavi told a story of ingenuity and enterprise.

I must note, that one of the most impressive aspects of Dharavi is the commitment to sustainability. The recycling industry, particularly plastic recycling, demonstrates an impressive effort towards environmental responsibility. It was so inspiring to witness how the residents have turned challenges into opportunities!!!! Something we can all learn from, especially me.

featured_reviews.name: Karen B
featured_reviews.review_text: Kashif was a very good guide when we did the “slum tour” even though we don’t like the term ,as the tour showed a working community. The only thing they don’t have is a university. Schools, dentist, doctors, banks, stores everything you need is there. Lots of entrepreneurial people working hard. Businesses like recycling, leather goods and metal smith are just a few of the businesses working in this community. Tour was vey informative and his English very good. We wish him good luck in his future plans.

As an european travelling to India (2nd time), I decided to use this agency to get a driver/guide, and facilitate me the many issues I could run into solo & by bus/train (talking from experience).
Yes, that's by far the way I recommend travelling, unless you're really adventurous and have plenty of spare time.

Once in Mumbai, I reached out with a few monuments/places/time frame I had in mind, and I got a schedule suggestion/quote which I was happy with. All is customizable in this country when it comes to tours!

The coordination was flawless.

Alam was the driver. The car was spacious and comfortable (not the classic Suzuki you see in Mumbai). We went to Ellora/Ajanta/Pune forts and various spots along the way. He is fluent in English, and I never had a single time of misunderstanding in 4 days. As he also works as guide, he was able to tell me tons of history abt each place, and I enjoy the conversation abt the many cultural questions I had abt India.

All this to say, I highly recommend this agency and their driver Alam.

If you have 2 days of free time in the mumbai region, I highly recommend Ajanta caves & Ellora caves (2 full days excursion). These two unesco world heritage sites are a must see

featured_reviews.review_text:
An Unforgettable and Eye Opening Tour with the Amazing Pooja!

Our tour of Dharavi with Magical Mumbai Tour was one of the absolute highlights of our time in the city, and it was made truly special by our fantastic guide, Pooja.
From the very beginning, Pooja was warm, knowledgeable, and incredibly passionate. She didn't just show us the sights; she shared stories and introduced us to the vibrant community spirit that makes Dharavi so unique. Her personal connection to the area allowed for an authentic and respectful experience that completely shattered our preconceptions. We learned so much about the recycling businesses, the local industries, and the daily lives of the resilient and hardworking people who live there.
If you are thinking about taking this tour, we cannot recommend it enough. For the best possible experience, you MUST ask for Pooja. Her insight, professionalism, and wonderful personality are what made this a five-star, truly unforgettable tour!

featured_reviews.name: Tanmay Kumar Mishra
featured_reviews.review_text:
Elephanta Caves, a UNESCO site near Mumbai, features stunning 5th–7th century rock-cut temples dedicated to Lord Shiva. The Trimurti sculpture is a highlight.

Pros:
•	Rich history and intricate carvings
•	Scenic ferry ride from Gateway of India
•	Cultural and spiritual significance

Cons:
•	Some areas need better maintenance
•	Can get crowded with persistent vendors
•	Requires a ferry ride and a steep climb

Tips:
•	Visit early to avoid crowds
•	Wear comfortable shoes and carry water
•	Watch out for monkeys

A must-visit for history lovers and architecture enthusiasts!

featured_reviews.name: Elise Nadeau
featured_reviews.review_text: My first time in India and Mumbai was my first stop. Found a 3 hour tour of Dhobi Ghat Laundry and Dharavi slums on “Get Your Guide” using this tour company and it did not disappoint! A young gentleman by the name of Abi was our guide. He took us to the Dhobi Ghat laundry site first for about an hour and then we proceeded to the Dharavi Slums for the remainder of the tour. Abi was an exceptional guide who I can’t recommend enough! He explained in great detail the history and process of the Dhobi Ghat which was fascinating to learn about. What was even more fascinating was the second half of the tour where we got to see first hand what daily life is like in the Dharavi Slums which is where our guide Abi grew up. It was very special to have a local guiding us around and giving us a rich detailed history of daily life on the inside.  Abi was very knowledgeable and answered any questions we had. He was also very patient with us as we stopped to take photos and speak to some of the locals. This tour was absolutely remarkable and eye opening and was definitely the highlight of my trip. An unforgettable experience that I highly recommend to anyone visiting Mumbai. Thank you Abi and Inside Mumbai Tours!

featured_reviews.name: Chris M.
featured_reviews.review_text:
First of all: Highly Recommended!!!

But let’s start from the beginning! As I am working for one of the biggest airline within Europe, I have visited so many places before, but India is somehow different, magical and mysterious.
I wanted to meet the people of Dharavi, see what their life/ daily business looks like. One of my colleagues recommended Inside Mumbai Tours (Mohammad) and I contacted him right away, he is super helpful and friendly, he organized the whole day and it was just beyond expectations.

Dharavi is about hard working people, family businesses, migrants from all over India hoping for a better life, making more money in Mumbai. It is about recycling, reusing and producing, about a great community that helps each other! About dancing kids in the monsoon rains and big smiles seeing foreigners talking and playing with them.

It is by far the most moving tour I did, it’s not about seeing poverty, it is about the challenge of life.

Our tour:
- Dharavi area
- dhobi ghat (washing place)
- Flower Market
- Victoria Station
- Train Ride
- Gateway of India

Mohammad is just the perfect Tour organizer, whatever you are interested in, he will organize the right tour for you, just text him!

Our tour guide was: Rakesh
He was so kind, helpful and patient at any time. He answered all our questions with so much knowledge, very good english and always a big smile! Thank you very much dear Rakesh for this great experience and possibility to meet people from your community.

Our tour included the pick-up and drop off at our Hotel, our driver: Mohideen! He drove super safe, very nice and comfortable ride with him! He explained some sights on the way to Dharavi and back!

Overall: I will definitely do another tour with Inside Mumbai Tours! I did many tours all around the world, but this was by far the best organization, the best tour guide and transportation! It was moving to have a insight into Dharavi and  to see daily life. I felt super safe, super welcomed and it was really interesting!

I recommended to all my colleagues!

Thank you very much for such an unforgettable trip and we would like to recommended friends or anyone interested going to Mumbai or Maharashtra.
